findings.status: confirmed in publisher version; already corrected by author
findings.title: Theorem3.3(2) and the potential-Sigma^0_2 part of Lemma6.5 fail

locations.anchor: Theorem3.3(2) and explicit dependency on Lemma6.5

findings.claim: A Polishable subgroup H in D(Pi^0_2)(G) has a potentially Sigma^0_2 coset relation; Lemma6.5 claims this even for Sigma^0_3 subgroups.
findings.construction: G=R^N with product topology; H=bv_0(R)={x:x_n ->0, sum |x_n-x_(n+1)|<infinity}. The tail-sum map from ell^1 is an isometric linear bijection onto H with variation norm, with continuous inclusion into G.
findings.hypotheses: G is Polish; H is an additive Polishable subgroup. Finite-variation sequences form F_sigma via closed partial-sum sublevels. L={liminf|x_n|=0} is G_delta. Finite variation implies convergence, so H=BV intersect L is in D(Pi^0_2), hence Sigma^0_3.
findings.decisive_evidence: If H were F_sigma, Baire category in its Banach norm would place a translated norm ball in a product-closed subset of H. Constant-c sequences truncated after m have variation norm c, but converge coordinatewise to a nonzero constant outside H, contradiction. For any Borel subgroup K<=P, potential Sigma^0_2 of E_K implies K is F_sigma: on a comeager continuity set of a Borel reduction, extend the relation to a union of closed D_j and express K as union_{j,i}{h:forall x in V_i,(x,xh) in D_j}. Each term is closed. Thus E_H is not potentially Sigma^0_2.
findings.proof_gap: Refining the topology to make the left H-action continuous and U_n closed does not establish closedness of all right translates U_n x. The map into the closed-set hyperspace is not justified. Hit-set measurability cannot establish closed-valuedness.
counterevidence_considered: The topology of H is not confused with its ambient subspace topology.
The subgroup is Polishable, not merely Borel.
The pointclass claim is membership; exact complexity of H need not be assumed.
The example satisfies the separate subgroup conclusion D(Pi^0_2), so it does not refute that separate clause.
A defect in an invoked lemma does not by itself refute every dependent theorem.
findings.impact: False theorem-level equivalence linking central complexity invariants, with an invalid lemma used in the classification proof. Major applies to exact frozen publisher bytes.
findings.repair_limits: Replace D(Pi^0_2) by Sigma^0_2 in Theorem3.3(2); both directions verified. Broader corrigendum classifications and operator constructions are author-documented and not all independently proved here.
findings.author_adoption: Existing authored corrigendum v3 dated2026-09-10; no contact or new-discovery claim.
findings.supporting_locations: Proposition2 and Example3, pp4–5; proof diagnosis, pp8–9.

independent_verification.evidence_positions: Original PDF5,12–14 / printed2201,2208–2210; author corrigendum v3 PDF4–5,8–11.
independent_verification.conditions: G=R^N in its Polish product topology; H=bv0(R) with its variation Banach topology. H is a Borel/Polishable subgroup, H belongs to D(Pi2) and hence Sigma3, satisfying the exact hypotheses. Potential complexity is interpreted via a Borel reduction/refinement; inversion relates the paper's coset convention to the one used in the corrected proof.
independent_verification.decisive_independent_check: The tail-sum map from l1 to H is an isometric bijection, with continuous inclusion because |x_n|<=variation norm. BV is the union of closed bounded-variation sublevels and L={liminf |x_n|=0} is Gdelta; finite variation implies convergence, so H=BV intersect L is D(Pi2). If H=union Cj with Cj product-closed, their inverse images are Banach-closed and Baire yields z+B(0,epsilon) contained in one Cj. For 0<c<epsilon the sequences (c,...,c,0,...) belong to Cj-z yet converge coordinatewise to the nonzero constant, outside H; contradiction. Independently, for any Borel subgroup K of a Polish group P, a reduction to an Fsigma equivalence relation is continuous on a comeager Gdelta C. Writing its pullback on C^2 as union(Dj intersect C^2), Dj closed, and Aj(h)={x:(x,xh) in Dj}, Baire shows h in K iff some Aj(h) has interior. Thus K=union_{j,i}{h: forall x in Vi,(x,xh) in Dj}, a countable union of closed sets. The reverse follows from the continuous difference map. Consequently the counterexample's relation cannot be potentially Sigma2.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The bv0 example satisfies H in D(Pi2), so it cannot refute the separate subgroup conclusion of Lemma6.5. That author's broader refutation uses a different operator construction, not independently certified here. The hyperspace hit-set calculation proves no closed-valuedness. Joint continuity of the full right G action cannot simply be appended because the identity orbit map would collapse the refinement to the original topology.
independent_verification.impact: An explicit theorem-level equivalence and its central proof lemma fail in the exact bound original publisher version. Theorem3.3 and Lemmas6.7/6.8 explicitly depend on6.5. Major does not require disproving the whole classification, and no blanket refutation of all dependent conclusions is asserted.
independent_verification.repair_boundary: The exact criterion is repaired by H in Sigma2, with both directions independently verified. The local closure/Delta3 replacement on corrigendum9–11 was checked with its necessary Pi3 hypothesis and Solecki-stage input; the later transfinite operator-range constructions and complete classification were not independently re-proved.

independent_acceptance.result: Confirmed: original Theorem 3.3(2) converse and the potential-Sigma2 conclusion of Lemma 6.5 fail. Major retained; report TeX/PDF unchanged. Existing author correction is acknowledged, not presented as a new discovery.
independent_acceptance.scope: Independent verification of the sole reported Problem, including both coset conventions, Polishability, Borel class membership, the quantified Baire-category counterexample, corrected necessary/sufficient criterion, exact gap in the original hyperspace map, proof dependencies and the limited Delta3 repair. The complete original and corrected transfinite classifications are not certified.

independent_analytic_reasoning: Checked the tail-sum inverse by telescoping and the zero-limit condition; every norm, Borel-class and product-topology assumption is operative.
Re-derived the Baire-category proof that bv0 is not Fsigma without using the disputed theorem or finite numerical approximations.
Re-derived the potential-Fsigma criterion for an arbitrary Borel subgroup; no normality or Polishability is needed for this criterion, and the coset convention is handled by inversion.

Checked the local-closure repair: an Fsigma intersect Gdelta representation gives a local Gdelta intersection by Baire; countable translates recover H. The Delta3 step uses the Pi3/Solecki condition, so it does not justify the original unrestricted Sigma3 assertion.
limitations: Focused independent acceptance of the reported Problem, not a complete formal reproof of every original or corrigendum theorem.
The later operator constructions and all corrected transfinite classifications were not independently established; their broader changes remain explicitly author-documented.
The separately acquired arXiv manuscript, original publisher PDF and dated corrigendum are not assumed scientifically identical.
No new author communication, no author code run, and no human adjudication.
